title: Ergonomic ranking bulk requests and resumable pages
creator: Priya Shah
description: Proposal and implementation plan to introduce a developer-friendly reranking request shape that supports bulk queries, explicit "k_mode" semantics (soft vs hard cutoffs), and resumable paged responses with an opaque, versioned cursor. Goal: improve UX for callers doing batched rerank work across many short queries while preserving repeatable ordering for resumptions and enabling streaming partial structured outputs for low-latency UX.
acceptance_criteria: New /v1/rerank endpoint accepts a bulk 'queries' array and returns per-query paged results with a 'cursor_v2' that can resume from the same logical position.
Ordering must be deterministic across resume when underlying documents haven't changed: tie-breaker is stable id-hash + original input index.
Support both 'hard' k_mode (exact top-k) and 'soft' k_mode (score threshold window + overfetch hint) with clear documented semantics.
Streaming response chunks include structured item records (id, score, provenance) and a progress marker; first-chunk latency <= 60ms P95 for typical small queries (N<=64) in hosted service tests.
Backward compatibility: legacy single-query shape and 'top_k' accepted and mapped to k_mode=hard with equivalent semantics.
Resume token (cursor_v2) is opaque, forward-compatible, and revokes after model/shard rollout that can affect determinism; API surface communicates 'resume_valid_until' if resume may be invalidated.
Integration tests covering resume across page boundaries, ordering stability, and streaming partial payload correctness added to rerank test harness.
implementation_notes: Request shape: { queries: [ { query_id, query_text, candidates: [candidate_id], group_key?, k, k_mode? } ], page_size?, cursor_v2? }.

k_mode values: 'hard' = truncate to exact k by score then tie-break; 'soft' = return >=k results until score delta < epsilon or max_overfetch reached. 'soft' flows used for quality-sensitive UX where caller does local thresholding.

Cursor_v2: base64 opaque payload versioned (v2), contains per-query last-seen score + deterministic tiebreak anchor (id-hash, original candidate index). Server validates resume against model+shard fingerprint; if mismatch, returns resume_invalid = true.

Streaming: use existing chunking transport (HTTP streaming/HTTP2) with an initial header frame containing metadata and subsequent frames carrying 'partial_page' objects; each item includes 'structured' fields: id, score, explain_tokens (optional), source_provenance array.
Batching: perform query-embedding batching then a coordinated rerank pass that can reuse embedding vectors across identical candidate ids; ensure memory bounds by chunking candidate lists internally.
Backwards compatibility shim to convert old single-query 'top_k' calls into the bulk shape with one query; log deprecation for callers that never send 'queries' array.
Telemetry: new counters for resume_success, resume_invalidated, streaming_first_byte_latency, and per-query overfetch_ratio to track 'soft' mode cost impact.
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor serialization/deserialization and forward/backward compatibility checks.
Integration tests: create synthetic dataset, request page 1, resume via cursor_v2 repeatedly across page boundaries, verify ordering identical to single-run unpaged result.
Load test: 500rps mixed bulk queries shape with keys Nqueries=8, Ncands=128 each; measure 95th latency and cost per query compared to baseline.
Streaming tests: validate partial structured payloads reconstructed client-side match full page payload once streaming completes.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'rerank_bulk_v2' initially in staging.
Canary deploy into 10% of hosted nodes for 48 hours with aggressive telemetry and kill-switch metric (resume_invalid_rate > 0.5% or streaming_first_byte_latency regression > 20%).
Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days pending stability and cost checks; notify key customers about cursor invalidation policy during model upgrades.
metrics: P95 first-chunk latency <= 60ms for queries where Ncand<=64 and page_size=10.
Resume validity rate >= 99.5% for queries where no document set change has occurred.
Overfetch ratio (soft mode) kept < 1.4 on average for production traffic after autotune.
Cost per served item tracked and compared against baseline to ensure no >10% increase in per-item GPU compute for typical workloads.
blockers: Final agreement on deterministic tie-breaker for equal scores across heterogeneous candidate lists (need legal/UX review for stable id hashing semantics).
Small serialization format edge cases between Go and Rust runtimes for opaque cursor payloads (interop PRs in progress).
